name: Eq-Obs correspondence (reader-family / indistinguishability Galois connection)

statement.note_ascii: For a declared experiment family E and a state relation R: E is admissible under R iff R refines the indistinguishability Eq(E) induced by E. This is the defining Galois-connection property between (Family, subseteq) and (Rel, subseteq).

definitions.Family: Experiment -> Prop (a declared set of experiments)
definitions.Eq(E): the indistinguishability relation induced by E: s ~ t iff every e in E agrees on s and t
definitions.Obs(R): the admissible-observable family for R: {e | R subseteq ker e}

claim_boundary: Generic finite/discrete mathematics only. No continuum premise, no Clay conclusion. Domain instantiation is a separate obligation.

name: Reader closure: extensive, monotone, idempotent, saturation-invariant

statement.note_ascii: The reader-saturation closure operator Cl is extensive, monotone, idempotent, and leaves the induced indistinguishability relation unchanged (saturation does not create or destroy distinctions).

claim_boundary: Generic finite/discrete mathematics only. No continuum premise, no Clay conclusion.

name: Future-reader equivalence is stable under a declared first action (dynamic weld congruence)

statement.note_ascii: All-future reader equivalence is a congruence with respect to every declared action: this is the relational well-definedness condition required before the quotient transition F_u^# can be named (CAN-006 commuting-square precondition).

definitions.FutureEq (~_Q): s ~_Q t iff every reader agrees on s and t after every future word of actions

claim_boundary: Generic finite/discrete mathematics only. Note: T4_dynamic_weld_well_defined is proof-identical to T3 and supplies only the congruence property; the literal quotient/projection/commuting-square instantiation is a separate, already-registered occurrence of CAN-006 (weld/M.02.v1) via T4b_quotient_commuting_square, merged information-discrete-math PR #131.

statement.note_ascii: For a candidate representation rho that is sufficient for a relation R, the kernel of rho (states rho maps identically) is contained in R. The corresponding factor-map existence is not duplicated here -- it is Toledo CAN-165.

definitions.SufficientFor(R): forall s t, rho s = rho t -> R s t

parents.derived_via: companion_to (factorisation supplied by CAN-165, not restated here)

statement.note_ascii: Adding experiments can only refine (never coarsen) the induced indistinguishability relation.

The indistinguishability induced by the union of two experiment families is exactly the intersection of the two separately-induced relations; this does not silently create any mixed/joint intervention -- mixed-action experiments must be declared explicitly.

name: Closed-reader binary meet/join laws

statement.latest: \operatorname{Cl}(E) \text{ is closed}; \quad A,B \text{ closed} \Rightarrow A \cap B \text{ closed}; \quad \operatorname{Cl}(A \cup B) \text{ is closed}
statement.note_ascii: Under a fixed admissible experiment universe, closed reader families form a binary meet/join structure: closure is itself closed, the intersection of two closed families is closed (binary meet), and the closure of the union of two families is closed (binary join).

definitions.ClosedFamily(E): Cl(E) is extensionally equal to E

claim_boundary: Generic finite/discrete mathematics only. No claim that every domain-specific bridge exists.

name: Safe finite strict-refinement termination (bounded-block-growth kernel)

statement.latest: (\forall P.\ b(P) \le N) \land (\lnot Closed(P) \Rightarrow b(P) < b(\mathrm{refine}(P))) \Rightarrow \forall P\ \exists k.\ Closed(\mathrm{refine}^k(P))
statement.note_ascii: If a partition's block count is bounded by N and every non-closed refinement step strictly increases the block count (with closedness decidable), then repeated refinement reaches a closed partition after finitely many steps. Proved by bounded strict growth / pigeonhole, no termination assumption is smuggled into the premise.

definitions.b(P): the block count of partition P
definitions.N: a fixed bound on block count

parents.derived_via: repairs (C.05.v1's current wrapper quantifies over arbitrary refine_step/is_closed and states unconditional termination, which is not provable as written; this is a strengthened statement with explicit finite-bound and strict-growth hypotheses, proposed as a superseding registration rather than a force-close of C.05.v1 per the founder's own instruction in toledo issue #36)

name: Stable finite-depth reader equivalence equals all-future reader equivalence

statement.note_ascii: If depth-n reader equivalence is a fixed point of one more step of refinement (DepthStable(n)), then depth-n equivalence is exactly all-future reader equivalence -- a finite, checkable witness for a claim that is a priori about infinitely many future steps.

definitions.DepthEq(n,s,t): s and t agree on every reader after every future word of length <= n
definitions.DepthStable(n): DepthEq(n) and DepthEq(n+1) coincide for every pair

name: Constructive firewall: A_con subseteq A_sem and constructive-closure invariance

statement.latest: \mathcal A_{\rm sem} := \mathcal A_{\rm ambient},\ \mathcal A_{\rm con} := \{e \in \mathcal A_{\rm ambient} \mid \mathrm{Constructive}(e)\};\quad \mathcal A_{\rm con} \subseteq \mathcal A_{\rm sem};\quad (E_1,E_2 \subseteq \mathcal A_{\rm con}) \land (\forall e.\ \mathrm{Constructive}(e) \Rightarrow (E_1\,e \iff E_2\,e)) \Rightarrow \operatorname{Eq}(E_1) = \operatorname{Eq}(E_2)
statement.note_ascii: A bookkeeping/closure fact about which sub-family of experiments EqOf is allowed to range over once membership is filtered by an abstract, uninterpreted resource predicate Constructive. No P-vs-NP-shaped claim, no computational-hardness premise or conclusion; domain instantiation of Constructive is a separate obligation. Not to be confused with the unrelated, still-open toledo registry/proposals/semantic_closure_accounting_p_vs_np_v0_1.json (PROP-SCA-PNP-01..06) cluster, which shares vocabulary but no theorem/proof/object.

definitions.Constructive: a fully abstract, uninterpreted predicate on experiments -- never instantiated, never given intro/elim rules beyond Family/EqOf
